title: Strategic Question Selection
tagline: Year 4 — Choosing which questions to attempt using chance of success, time cost and marks, including negative marking

introduction.overview: Question selection refines triage with probability. Each question has marks, a time cost and a chance that you solve it correctly. Its expected value is chance × marks minus (1 − chance) × penalty, and its value per minute divides that by the time. Attempting questions in descending order of expected value per minute maximises the expected score. The estimates are rough, but the habit of asking "what is my chance?" prevents poor choices.
introduction.placementRelevance: Sectional-cutoff tests with negative marking reward selective attempts.
introduction.realWorldContext: Choosing projects by expected payoff per unit effort is the same idea.

learningObjectives: Compute expected marks of a question
Set a minimum confidence for attempting

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Expected marks = p × m − (1 − p) × n, where p is the chance of being correct, m the marks and n the penalty.

coreDefinitions: Chance of success: your estimated probability of being correct.
Expected marks: average marks if repeated many times.
Penalty: marks lost for a wrong answer.
Break-even chance: p where expected marks are zero.
Value per minute: expected marks ÷ time.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: A question is worth attempting when its expected value is positive and its rate is higher than your alternatives.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Estimate p, compute p × m − (1 − p) × n, divide by minutes, and rank.

mainNarrative: A question you will get right with probability 0.6, worth 1 mark with a 0.25 penalty: expected marks = 0.6 − 0.4 × 0.25 = 0.5.
Break-even chance = 0.25 ÷ 1.25 = 20%. Attempt whenever your chance exceeds 20%.
A question with p = 0.9 taking 45 seconds has expected value 0.9 − 0.025 = 0.875, a rate of 1.17 per minute.
A question with p = 0.5 taking 150 seconds: expected 0.5 − 0.125 = 0.375, rate 0.15 per minute.
Rank by rate: attempt the first before the second.

deepDiveAspects.title: Calibration
deepDiveAspects.content: Your estimated p is often too high; track your actual accuracy on mocks.

deepDiveAspects.title: Penalty-free sections
deepDiveAspects.content: If there is no penalty, attempt every question; the break-even chance is 0.

solvedExamples.title: Rate
solvedExamples.question: Expected marks 0.875 in 45 seconds. Rate per minute?

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Estimate p, compute expected marks and rate, and attempt in descending order of rate.

placementTips.recruiterInsight: Your honest p is the key input.
